Five modules

The interfaces encapsulate storage, scheduling and source formats. Internal processing stages remain within their owning modules.

Sattle.ModelIdentity, values, ontology and graph changes.↗Sattle.ProjectionsPortable definitions, typed expressions and compilation.↗Sattle.RuntimeAsync ingestion, graph access, configuration and commits.↗Sattle.AdaptersNative source formats and graph observations.↗Sattle.DocumentsStable document structure, patches and rendering.↗

Master and derived graphs

A graph space declares the master. Derived graphs bind master or upstream outputs by name, with separate input and output ontology pins. Each derived graph records the versions it consumed.

Verification scope

The contracts compile with warnings treated as errors. Selected finite examples exercise diff laws, stable identities, lens laws, document edits, recursion and cross-ontology composition. Invalid fixtures demonstrate rejection.

Production execution, general transformation correctness, distributed consistency, throughput and bounded memory remain unverified. The open-work checklist tracks these obligations.
